doc.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019

title: Explaining music to non-musician teachers
summary: Both talk about learning to avoid musical jargon when working with classroom teachers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I totally agree and I learned so much from working with like — I had the same exact scenario working with classroom teachers. And there’s nothing like getting their — the questions they ask or the — like I remember doing a thing one day and I kept using the word “melody.” Finally, bless her heart, some teacher said, like, excuse me but, “What’s a melody?” And it was like this, oh man, this realization, that, find a way to not just use your own lingo. And boy that was very valuable.

Right. And you know so you can’t communicate directly, like that. So you sit and find a way maybe to find some commonality and what happens is then you can cultivate an exchange. An exchange that wouldn’t have happened otherwise.
And the feeling that you have exchanging and knowing a little bit more about each other wouldn’t have happened. That’s why it’s important.
